source: California AB 2013 (Generative AI: Training Data Transparency Act) — Google's AI Training Data Transparency Summary
rows: The following reflects Google’s efforts to prepare a high-level summary of the training data used to develop our generative AI systems and services in an accurate and comprehensive manner. Ads AI Studio Android Chrome Fi Fitbit Flow Gemini Apps Gemini Education Gemini in Workspace Home/Nest Lookout Maps Marketing Nest Notebook LM Pixel Photos Play Search Shopping Wallet YouTube Our systems are powered by thinking models, capable of reasoning before responding, resulting in enhanced performance and improved accuracy. The underlying models are well-suited for applications that require enhanced reasoning, advanced coding, multimodal understanding and long context, as examples. The datasets used for model development are acquired with the intention of furthering these intended purposes. The first date a dataset was used during the development of a generative AI system or service pre-dates January 2022.

The training datasets are characterized by their large-scale and diverse nature, designed to enable the models to comprehend vast datasets and handle complex problems from various information sources, including data sourced from publicly available datasets, licensed data obtained via commercial licensing agreements, data obtained by crawlers, data collected from our users and also user interactions with the models (in accordance with the relevant terms, policies, and pursuant to user controls, where appropriate), other datasets that Google acquires or generates in the course of its business operations or directly from its workforce, and synthetically generated data. Datasets may include or reference material that is subject to copyright, trademark, or patent protection, and these datasets are used under applicable licenses or pursuant to law. Some of the datasets also include aggregate consumer information and/or personal information. For example, there are instances when we use data collected from users of Google products and services, along with user interactions with the models, in accordance with Google’s relevant terms of service, privacy policy, service-specific policies, and pursuant to user controls, where appropriate. We nonetheless employ measures designed to minimize personal information in these datasets where appropriate prior to training, in accordance with law and our policies.
The models are trained on a large corpus of training data sets representing more than 1 trillion tokens of text, 1 billion images, 1 million hours of video, and 1 million hours of audio.

The cleaning and preprocessing of data to make it suitable for training involved, on a case-by-case basis, filtering irrelevant or harmful content, text, and other modalities (e.g., filtering content that is violative of CSAM laws).
